A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same principal-subspace orthogonal fine-tuning work, renamed from MOFT to PSOFT. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original MOFT evaluations on language and vision tasks, memory and runtime measurements, and ablations. Some GLUE baseline scores are attributed to prior work, but the paper's own empirical results are clearly identifiable.

after.justification: v2 reports original PSOFT evaluations, efficiency measurements, and orthogonality and Neumann-series ablations in Section 5 and the appendices. Retained results from v1 also qualify.

M1.justification: The SVD decomposition, frozen principal projections and residual weights, orthogonal adaptation matrix, and two scaling vectors remain. v2 changes Cayley inverse computation to a truncated Neumann series with K=5 (Section 5). Section 4.3 also proposes an optional orthogonality-error constraint without establishing its use. Renaming and expanded pseudocode do not introduce the scaling vectors anew.

E1.justification: v2 explicitly omits MNLI and QQP from GLUE evaluation, reducing reported coverage from 37 to 35 tasks (Appendix F). The remaining GLUE tasks, 19 VTAB tasks, eight commonsense benchmarks, and GSM-8K/MATH coverage remain. Larger parameter budgets and different model configurations do not add task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds or updates GOFTv2, qGOFTv2, and OFTv2 within the task comparisons, including reported OOM outcomes. BOFT and PiSSA enter the GLUE comparison, and PiSSA enters VTAB. SVFT disappears from the encoder comparisons and FacT-TT/FacT-TK disappear from VTAB, while SVFT remains in the low-budget language-model appendices.

E3.justification: GLUE changes from original validation-set reporting to an equal validation/test subdivision with checkpoint selection on the new validation subset (v2 Appendix F). Sequence lengths, epochs, and adaptation ranks also change. New larger-budget language-model comparisons supplement retained low-budget settings, broaden BOFT module insertion, and report FP32 for FFT instead of v1's BF16 exception.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons of unconstrained, softly regularized, and strictly orthogonal adaptation at matched ranks or parameter counts (Table 6), plus Neumann-term sensitivity (Figure 8b). It revises efficiency analyses and removes one initialization variant and the displayed MATH scaling-vector results. The SVD and rank sweeps are retained; the module-insertion analysis is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means for GLUE and VTAB, but v2 removes v1 Appendix M and Tables 17–18, which supplied standard deviations. No replacement uncertainty estimates appear. This substantially reduces variability reporting without establishing any change in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds larger-budget results, including PSOFT r=352 scoring 63.08/15.98 on GSM-8K/MATH and r=424 averaging 82.54 on commonsense reasoning (Tables 4–5). Many earlier low-budget results survive in Tables 13 and 15, so these are not same-setting gains. Encoder results, efficiency outcomes, and ablation entries also change. Identical VTAB LoRA r=8 task scores receive different averages: 68.8 in v1 versus 71.8 in v2.

T1.justification: v1's angle-only equivalence becomes an angle-and-norm preservation theorem with explicit nonzero-column assumptions in v2 Appendix B. Its necessity proof now uses norm preservation and a right inverse of B, repairing the earlier unsupported inference from equal angles. v1's PL convergence analysis and full-space lifting proof are removed, while v2 adds an equal-budget effective-rank derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from memory-efficient orthogonal adaptation preserving hyperspherical energy to simultaneously achieving semantic preservation, expressiveness, and parameter, memory, and computational efficiency. v2's abstract and introduction explicitly claim higher effective rank and preservation of both angles and norms. This broadens the scientific promise beyond the MOFT-to-PSOFT renaming.

C2.justification: v1's gradient-noise and stability rationale and detailed Cayley-runtime caveats are dropped. v2 develops explanations based on higher effective rank, interprets strict orthogonality as improving parameter efficiency, discusses validation/test reliability, and interprets Neumann approximation through its speed–accuracy tradeoff. These revise the paper's mechanism explanations and evaluation qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a PSOFT-specific public-code link, specifies the Neumann approximation setting and CUDA peak-memory measurement function, and updates rank/learning-rate tables. Its pseudocode now includes the already-existing scaling vectors. v1's absolute throughput/runtime tables are removed, although SVD initialization timings remain. Most library, hardware, and data-processing information is retained.

R1.justification: New references include OFTv2, AdaLoRA, semantic-drift work, and studies motivating the revised GLUE evaluation; FacT and PL-convergence references disappear. Related work refines the distinction from AdapterR into spectral versus geometric preservation. These are substantive but bounded updates within the retained PEFT/OFT literature.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of related work and methodology are rewritten. Methodology gains three explicit design subsections, experiments are reorganized around encoder-only and decoder-only models, and the algorithm and module-insertion analysis move into a extensively reorganized appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds a qualitative comparison table and a geometric method diagram, restructures benchmark tables with parameter/memory columns and OOM rows, and introduces colored highlighting. Efficiency displays are reorganized into Figure 4, the scaling-vector plot becomes a GSM-8K-only bar chart, and Figure 8 combines the relocated insertion plot with a new Neumann plot. Page styling and text wrapping also change extensively.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs the central necessity proof, separates GLUE model selection from testing, and adds relevant OFT comparisons and mechanism ablations. However, it removes reported variability estimates and introduces inconsistent VTAB aggregation: unchanged LoRA scores acquire an average of 71.8 instead of 68.8, while FFT retains its earlier aggregation. These gains in theoretical and evaluation rigor coexist with reduced empirical reporting reliability, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
